Former Haas Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean has apologised to Zak Brown after "misunderstanding" Brown's comments on Oscar Piastri in Madrid . Grosjean attended the Spanish GP as a pundit for French television station Canal+ alongside appearing on F1 TV . The ex-F1 driver was in screen during an F1 TV interview with McLaren boss Zak Brown after qualifying at the Madring where Lando Norris took pole position. Oscar Piastri qualified in P7, four tenths behind his teammate. “I think you’ve got Lando on his A-plus game, so I don’t think there was anything left lap-time-wise there and so he found that," Brown said. “Oscar has been right there with him all weekend and just didn’t get that same extra [performance] that lap. “We’ll continue to look at it. He’ll look at the data and probably do what we all did and go: ‘Wow, what a lap!” Oscar Piastri did not have a successful race at the Madring Grosjean admits to Zak Brown misunderstanding on Oscar Piastri remarks During his Spanish GP commentary with Canal+ the next day, Grosjean claimed that Brown had been heavily critical of Piastri, adding that Brown had said Norris is a world champion and better driver than Piastri. On Sunday evening, Grosjean posted an apology to social media, admitting that he had misinterpreted the McLaren boss' words. The post read: “Today, I made a comment on Canal Plus F1 regarding Zak Brown’s comments about Oscar Piastri during an interview yesterday on F1 TV, which I was part of. “I completely misunderstood his words and want to apologise for that. I know how important it is to Zak and the entire McLaren team to respect their drivers and treat them fairly and equally. “McLaren had the fastest car today and were unlucky with the VSC. I’m sure both Lando and Oscar will have another chance to fight for the win in Baku.” Unfortunate Virtual Safety Car timing and a long pit stop deprived Norris and McLaren of a win in Madrid, with the reigning World Champion eventually finishing third. items.article_search_text: The Australian finished eighth after suffering front wing damage on the first lap from contact with Russell. The bad timing of the Virtual Safety Car and a complicated qualifying session hampered his race at Madring. Oscar Piastri lived a real ordeal at the Spanish Grand Prix. The Australian McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren] driver, who arrived in Madrid hoping to score important points, was forced to settle for eighth position after a race marked by damage to his car and a series of adverse circumstances that prevented him from showing his true potential. The problem began on the first lap, Piastri was involved in an incident with George Russell [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/tyre-overheating-cost-george-russell-in-madrid-mercedes-driver-reveals] when the Briton's Mercedes crossed into his path toward the barriers, the Australian had nowhere to go and suffered damage to his front wing, specifically the endplate, which made him lose downforce for the rest of the race, the team was able to mitigate the problem at his only pit stop, but not fully solve it. "It was quite painful, obviously, from lap 1, there wasn't much I could do from there" declared Piastri after the race. The Australian also pointed to the bad luck with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car: "The VSC timing certainly wasn't ideal for us, we stayed on the hards and it was a difficult afternoon" he explained. F1 Spanish Grand Prix: Antonelli Takes Victory in an Uneventful Madrid Race [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/bd727c6d-9645-49e9-8c31-d602dfb11e57.jpeg] F1 Spanish Grand Prix: Antonelli Takes Victory in an Uneventful Madrid Race Kimi Antonelli extends his championship lead with a patient and calculated race in the Spanish Grand Prix. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-spanish-grand-prix-antonelli-takes-victory-in-an-uneventful-madrid-race] Piastri had chosen not to pit under the VSC, betting on a long stint strategy in the hope of a later Safety Car or red flag. However, there were no further incidents and he was forced to make his stop in race conditions, which made him lose time and come out in traffic. Although he managed an overtake on Arvid Lindblad, one of the few of the day, he could not get past Franco Colapinto's Alpine in the final laps. To understand Piastri's difficulties, you have to go back to Saturday's qualifying, the Australian needed an extra set of soft tires to secure his place in Q2, which left him as the only front running driver with a used set of the C4 compound for his first Q3 lap. On his second attempt with new tires he made a mistake at the start of the lap and could only qualify seventh, which left him in the middle of the pack, an always dangerous position at the narrow first corner of Madring. F1 Daily: A Chaotic F3 Crash at Madrid, Norris's Super Lap, and Sainz's Penalty [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/f26232b4-2d99-4e67-b08a-f14b8d25572f.jpeg] F1 Daily: A Chaotic F3 Crash at Madrid, Norris's Super Lap, and Sainz's Penalty A chaotic crash at a Formula 3 race started things off the wrong way at the Madring. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-daily-a-chaotic-f3-crash-at-madrid-norriss-super-lap-and-sainzs-penalty] "It was mainly the end of qualifying and then lap 1, obviously it was far from ideal, with damage throughout the race, it was hard like that, but today we tried to learn as much as possible to get more out of the car and out of my driving, hopefully we have learned some things for the rest of the year" summarized Piastri. The 2026 season is being a constant contrast for Piastri. While his teammate Lando Norris accumulates five podiums, two wins, three poles and a Sprint win, the Australian has only two podiums, the last in Miami and a third place in a Sprint. In the championship, Norris is 66 points ahead of him, a difference that reflects Piastri's difficulty in finding consistency. The Australian hopes his luck will change soon. The next round in Baku in two weeks gives him a chance for redemption. Last year Azerbaijan was the scene where his championship hopes suffered a hard blow after an early retirement, something Piastri will want to make up for when the Formula 1 paddock gathers again on the streets of the Azerbaijani capital.

Oscar Piastri received a black-and-white flag from the FIA during Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix for exceeding track limits, and admitted afterwards that he'd overstepped. The McLaren driver was carrying front-wing damage after first-lap contact with George Russell's Mercedes, which affected the car for the rest of the race. He finished eighth, his worst result since 11th in Canada. Piastri said the contact happened when Russell kept squeezing him toward the wall. He braked to avoid him, and both cars ended up bunched together. He said it was "easy to go a little bit too far" on a track with no kerb or wall on the inside of some corners. "It was just a tough afternoon from literally the start,” Piastri reflected to the media, including Motorsport Week . "From then on, the rest of the race was very compromised, obviously with some of the damage and the track position mainly.” "I was alongside, and he just kept squeezing me to the wall, and then I hit the brakes and kind of avoided him. But amongst all that, he hit the brakes as well. Everyone hit the brakes, and we kind of got stuck together and everything.” "I was just expecting a bit more space, and obviously between a car and a wall, you can't make any more space, so that was tricky.” "On a track like this, you're always searching for a bit of clean air in the high-speed corners, and with no kerb or wall on the inside of some of the corners, it's very easy to just go a little bit too far." Despite the finish, Piastri felt he'd had a decent race in clean air, but said getting stuck behind a train of cars after the pit stops, including Franco Colapinto's Alpine, cost him further. He said the medium tyre was good for one lap and then fell away badly. "I think the pace and clean air on the hard was pretty good, but we were trying to make up the pit loss of the VSC to the guys who pitted, and once they got the loss back, I was stuck again, so that was painful," said Piastri. "Then when we pitted onto the medium, we pitted into a four-car train, and that wasn't great, and the medium tyre was just awful. "It was good for [one lap], and then it was pretty terrible, so a lot of things to try and fix."

items.article_search_text: No one was happy and even the winner admitted he didn’t deserve to win after some ‘insanely unlucky’ drama. 7NEWS brings you the latest local news from Australia and around the world. Stay up to date with all of the breaking sport, politics, entertainment, finance, weather and business headlines. Today's news, live updates & all the latest breaking stories from 7NEWS. Wonder boy Kimi Antonelli has roared ever closer to the world Formula 1 crown with victory around the new Madrid street circuit — but there was nothing but gloom for McLaren as Lando Norris got “insanely unlucky” and Oscar Piastri’s wretched season continued with an eighth-place finish in a damaged car. Antonelli took another huge stride towards becoming the youngest world champion ever with his Spanish Grand Prix victory, but even the 20-year-old was happy to concede he had got seriously fortunate on Sunday (Monday AEST) to oust third-placed Norris. “I feel a bit bad for Lando, he deserved to win,” shrugged Antonelli, after he took full advantage of Lance Stroll putting his Aston Martin in the wall on the 14th lap to earn a free pit-stop during a Virtual Safety Car period. Meanwhile, world champion Norris, who’d been looking unstoppable seven seconds ahead at the front, had just passed the pit entry, and missed a chance of a cheap tyre change. Piastri was not even really at the races once his McLaren collided twice on the opening lap with George Russell’s Mercedes, and he ended up having to battle through the race with a damaged front wing. McLaren decided not to change it because time would be lost but just altered the angle to provide more downforce when a disgruntled-sounding Piastri eventually pitted on lap 42. Emerging in 11th place, he fought to get back among the points but it will still dismay him to end up a minute-and-a-half slower than his teammate. “It was pretty painful, obviously from lap one,” sighed Piastri, who reckoned the real damage had come by finishing seventh in qualifying. “Not much I really could have done from that first lap, having damage for the whole race. It was just a difficult afternoon.” Norris dropped to fifth after a slow front-right tyre change when he did stop under the VSC and could only make up two places on the new Madring circuit where overtaking is at a premium. “I don’t know how someone looks at this design and goes, mint!” Norris said. Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto added: “I almost fell asleep.” Fernando Alonso said it was “sad” that the key feature of the track — the banked Monumental corner — was so easy in these cars his Aston Martin team press officer could drive it flat-out. All the drivers rued the lack of overtaking opportunities and hoped for layout changes, particularly with the turn 5-6 chicane, before the next visit in 2027. Beyond the entertainment of it all Carlos Sainz also said there was little thought to driver safety. The Madring follows the fast but walled street circuit template put forward by Baku, Jeddah and Las Vegas in more recent years. “It seems like the FIA is happy to go in this direction moving forward in terms of new circuits, which obviously, as drivers, we are raising our, not concerns, but our point of wanting to keep improving safety,” the Williams driver said. “We’re going to go towards these circuits because going at 260km/h, 270km/h on esses that you cannot see through is definitely eye-opening and definitely makes you question how safe everything is.” Despite his superior pace in the first race to be held in Madrid for 45 years prompting team boss Zak Brown to say he’d been in “a league of his own”, Norris couldn’t pass Max Verstappen for second, even though he felt the Dutchman had illegally run off the road while defending his position on the penultimate lap. So Verstappen finished runner-up, 4.3sec behind the Italian winner, with polesitter Norris third just seven-tenths back. “Insanely unlucky with the Virtual Safety Car ... I was the only once who didn’t get a chance to do the pit stop there. Of course I feel like I deserved more,” Norris sighed, before suggesting the lottery of pitting under the VSC needed to be changed. Charles Leclerc was fourth, and Russell fifth as Antonelli extended his advantage in the championship race with an eighth win of the year to 81 points with nine rounds remaining. Lewis Hamilton’s fading championship hopes also suffered further when he retired early on with a brake problem. He’s now 101 points behind Antonelli, 20 behind Russell and five ahead of fourth-placed Norris. Charles Leclerc is fifth, Verstappen sixth and Piastri seventh, now a whopping 172 points off the lead. — with 7NEWS Journalist from Australian news agency, Australian Associated Press.

Follow along for all the action. Max Verstappen has been told to give Lewis Hamilton his place back, after running wide during an earlier lap. He’s responded with his typical colourful language but has relented. “Mate, what the f-— are you guys talking about. He would have shunted,” he said. “Like what are you guys talking about. If I just stay on the track, I am out of the race”. Meanwhile, a flying Lando Norris is leading the pack, with Kimi Antonelli in second. Oscar Piastri’s increasingly underwhelming Formula One season has taken another turn for the worse in Madrid with a “pretty shocking” qualifying lap at the Spanish Grand Prix. Doubtless making the Australian even more frustrated on Saturday was that his hugely disappointing seventh-place finish in qualifying on the new Madring street circuit came as teammate Lando Norris delivered a pole-grabbing lap hailed by McLaren’s team boss as a “masterpiece”. The world champion produced his dazzling lap in the sunshine from seemingly nowhere, clocking a 1min 31.82sec circuit to edge Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli by just 0.011sec, with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen third and Ferrari’s ‌Lewis Hamilton fourth. But while a “shocked” Norris was hailing what he called “probably one of the best laps I’ve done”, it was back to the drawing board for Piastri, who was disappointed to only finish in 1:32.294 — remarkably, nearly half a second behind his teammate. “The first lap wasn’t too bad but the second lap was pretty shocking. Disappointing,” sighed the 25-year-old, who could find it difficult to make much headway from seventh on Sunday on an unforgiving, tight circuit where, he admitted, overtaking “will be difficult”. He’s keeping up a brave face, though, still talking up how he hopes to earn a victory somewhere this year to set himself up for a realistic crack at the title in 2027. Piastri hasn’t won a race since the Dutch Grand Prix now over a year ago when he was leading the 2025 championship, but he’s adamant his subsequent dramatic fall off wasn’t a factor in his disappointing 2026 campaign “Of course, I would love to win a race ‌or two this year, ‌or more if I can. But for me, honestly, the biggest thing, the end goal is to ​try and win championships. And if I can’t do that this year, then I want to make sure I’m as best prepared as I can for next year,” he explained. For the moment, though, that still seems a long way off as his smooth driving style just doesn’t seem to be suited by the vast changes to the 2026 F1 cars. “It’s all to do with ‌technically driving the car. There’s nothing to do with a hangover from last year ... it’s very much a technical thing,” he explained. “It’s not like I’m slow, feeling sorry for myself or thinking about last year. It’s just that a few of the weekends I’ve had to drive the car in a different way that just hasn’t really worked for me. “The biggest thing this year has been the cars are very different to drive, both from a power unit point of view but also the car itself is fundamentally very ​different and the tyres also. “You’ve got to drive it ​very differently and I would say it’s not ⁠necessarily in the way that I would choose to drive a race car. So there’s just been some struggles getting ​to grips with that.” Meanwhile, though, Norris does seem to be getting to grips with it, producing “one of those laps where everything pretty much worked perfectly.” The champion’s 19th career pole and third of the season was hailed by McLaren team boss Andrea Stella as a “masterpiece” which could only have been bettered if he hadn’t made a mistake at the very last corner that possibly cost him 0.3sec. Norris had been only sixth after the first run in the third qualifying session but he diced daringly with the wall during the breathtaking final lap, and declared over the radio at the end: “Oh, what a lap, gorgeous ... oh, that might be my best one.” Journalist from Australian news agency, Australian Associated Press.

Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027. That means winning at least one race to help rescue a disappointing year after the highs of 2025 and, with leaders Mercedes disappearing over the horizon, helping champions McLaren beat Ferrari to second place in the constructors’ standings. The 25-year-old was 31 points clear of British teammate Lando Norris, the eventual champion, at the top after the September 7 Italian Grand Prix last year and had won seven of 16 races. Piastri left Monza this year still without a win to his credit after 13 rounds and 151 points behind Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli but fifth in that race and feeling he had taken “a much better step in the right direction. “Of course, I would love to win a race or two this year, or more if I can,” he told Reuters at the Spanish Grand Prix. “But for me, honestly, the biggest thing, the end goal is to try and win championships. And if I can’t do that this year, then I want to make sure I’m as best prepared as I can for next year.” REASONABLE CHANCE OF BEATING FERRARI Piastri’s best result in the first season of the sport’s new engine and rules era has been second place behind Antonelli in Japan last March, while teammate Lando Norris has won twice. The Australian started the season with two ‘did not starts’, including one at home in Melbourne. “Never say never but it is going to be incredibly challenging for the championship,” said the Australian with typical deadpan understatement. “(We’re) trying to do the best we can in the constructors’ championship because, whilst I think beating Mercedes is going to be tricky, I think we do have a reasonable chance of trying to beat Ferrari. Just trying to win races if we can and learn as much as we can for next year.” Ferrari are currently second, 59 points ahead of McLaren. Mercedes are 122 further in front. Piastri’s 2025 season nose-dived from a point where he seemed destined to take the title to being overtaken by Norris and then Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, ending up third overall. His most recent win was the Dutch Grand Prix in August last year. The Australian denied that the knock-on effects of that campaign, and the mental toll of coming to terms with the crown slipping through his hands in what might even have been the opportunity of a lifetime, had seeped over into 2026. “It’s all to do with technically driving the car. There’s nothing to do with a hangover from last year … it’s very much a technical thing,” he said. “It’s not like I’m slow, feeling sorry for myself or thinking about last year. It’s just that a few of the weekends I’ve had to drive the car in a different way that just hasn’t really worked for me. “The biggest thing this year has been the cars are very different to drive, both from a power unit point of view but also the car itself is fundamentally very different and the tyres also. There’s just been a lot of challenges around that and how you extract performance out of the car. “You’ve got to drive it very differently and I would say it’s not necessarily in the way that I would choose to drive a race car. So there’s just been some struggles getting to grips with that.”

items.article_search_text: ​Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams ‌effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to ​give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027. F1: Oscar Piastri still hoping to win races to set up 2027 title bid left “Of course, I would love to win a race or two this year, or more if I can,” said Piastri. REUTERS REUTERS https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/abjfxu/article71460630.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/2026-09-05T082724Z_1195120289_UP1EM950NHM2G_RTRMADP_3_MOTOR-F1-ITALY.JPG JAKUB PORZYCKI Formula One F1 - Italian Grand Prix - Autodromo Nazionale Monza, Monza, Italy - September 5, 2026 McLaren's Oscar Piastri arrives ahead of practice REUTERS/Jakub Porzycki Oscar Piastri left Monza this year still without ‌a win to his credit after 13 rounds and 151 points behind Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli MADRID ​Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams ‌effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to ​give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027. That means winning at least ⁠one race to help rescue a disappointing year after the highs of 2025 and, with leaders Mercedes disappearing over the horizon, helping champions McLaren beat Ferrari to second place in the constructors’ standings. The 25-year-old was 31 points clear of British ‌teammate Lando Norris, the eventual champion, at the top after the September 7 Italian Grand Prix last year and had won seven of 16 races. Piastri left Monza this year still without ‌a win to his credit after 13 rounds and 151 points behind Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli ‌but ⁠fifth in that race and feeling he had taken “a much better step in the ⁠right direction. “Of course, I would love to win a race or two this year, or more if I can,” he told Reuters at the Spanish Grand Prix. “But for me, honestly, the biggest thing, the end goal is to try and win championships. And if I ​can’t do that this year, then I ‌want to make sure I’m as best prepared as I can for next year.” REASONABLE CHANCE OF BEATING FERRARI Piastri’s best result in the first season of the sport’s new engine and rules era has been second place behind Antonelli in Japan last March, while teammate Lando Norris has won twice. ALSO READ | Lewis Hamilton crashes in final Spanish GP practice https://sportstar.thehindu.com/motorsport/f1/lewis-hamilton-crash-spanish-gp-final-practice-ferrari-madrid/article71460081.ece The Australian started the ‌season with two ‘did not starts’, including one at home in Melbourne. “Never say never but it is ​going to be incredibly challenging for the championship,” said the Australian with typical deadpan understatement. “(We’re) trying to do the best we can in the constructors’ championship because, whilst I ⁠think beating Mercedes is going to be tricky, I think we do have a reasonable chance of trying to beat Ferrari. Just trying to win races if we can and learn as much as we can for ‌next year.” Ferrari are currently second, 59 points ahead of McLaren. Mercedes are 122 further in front. Piastri’s 2025 season nose-dived from a point where he seemed destined to take the title to being overtaken by Norris and then Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, ending up third overall. His most recent win was the Dutch Grand Prix in August last year. The Australian denied that the knock-on effects of that campaign, and the mental toll of coming to terms with the crown slipping through his hands in what might even have been the opportunity of a ‌lifetime, had seeped over into 2026. “It’s all to do with technically driving the car. There’s nothing to do with a hangover from ​last year ... it’s very much a technical thing,” he said. “It’s not like I’m slow, feeling sorry for myself or thinking about last year. It’s just that a few of the ⁠weekends I’ve had to drive the car in a different way that just hasn’t really worked for me. “The biggest ⁠thing this year has been the cars are very different to drive, both from a power unit point of view but also the car itself is fundamentally very different and the tyres ‌also. There’s just been a lot of challenges around that and how you extract performance out of the car. “You’ve got to drive it very differently and I would say it’s not necessarily in the ​way that I would choose to drive a race car. So there’s just been some struggles getting to grips with that.”

items.article_search_text: Andrea Stella defends the philosophy of letting his drivers compete, but admits that the internal battle cost them time against Verstappen. The team will review the clash to see if they could have managed it better and optimized the final result. The Italian Grand Prix left a new chapter in the relationship between the McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]drivers. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri had a tense duel in the final stages of the race that ended with the Briton putting two wheels on the grass and accusing his teammate of having pushed him off track. After this episode, Andrea Stella, the team principal, has assured that McLaren will review the incident to determine if they could have managed the situation better. The altercation occurred in the final laps of the race, when both drivers were fighting for fourth position. Norris overtook Piastri on lap 48 but the Australian recovered the position one lap later. The Briton tried to return the overtake but found a gap that was closing and ended up with two wheels on the grass, suggesting that Piastri "pushed me off." The tension was evident on the team radio. Stella, however, downplayed the incident: "When we reviewed it I think we saw that the episode is much more benign than it might have seemed in the heat of the moment" declared the Italian. The McLaren boss explained that the decision not to interfere in the fight between his drivers was intentional: "The two cars were on the same tires, the same tire age, the same car, so we thought there was no need to interfere in the normal development of the race. We let them compete, we believe it was the right thing to do" he stated. F1 Daily: Antonelli's Monza Miracle, Hamilton's Frustration, and Audi's Protest [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/0e98c448-e7bd-4879-939b-9f6f37e9f416.jpeg] F1 Daily: Antonelli's Monza Miracle, Hamilton's Frustration, and Audi's Protest Alpine's Pierre Gasly delivered one of the best, most surprisingly good qualifying performances this season. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-daily-antonellis-monza-miracle-hamiltons-frustration-and-audis-protest] The team has a history of internal reviews after the Monza race. Last year, McLaren's famous "papaya rules" were under the spotlight when Piastri was ordered to let Norris pass. On this occasion, the analysis will focus on whether the internal battle cost them a better position against their rivals: "I think you're right to highlight that as soon as you fight with your teammate, you can lose time. So, was there a better way for McLaren to face Max Verstappen? We will review it" admitted Stella. The Dutchman from Red Bull was the big beneficiary of the duel between the McLarens. Verstappen managed to overtake both to take the third step of the podium behind the Mercedes of George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. Stella acknowledged the superiority of the Red Bull: "I think overall Max was faster, he just got caught in that hook you have this year when you lose the tow here at Monza and you have to use energy to defend yourself from someone else" he explained. Norris and His Salary Gap With Hamilton and Verstappen [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/3392ea03-9ac6-49b7-9c78-3fcd2fa90ff7.jpeg] Norris and His Salary Gap With Hamilton and Verstappen The world champion acknowledged that he had a raise after renewing, but denied astronomical figures. He states that his rivals' track records justify their million dollar contracts, although he trusts he can match them in the future with his on track performance. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/norris-and-his-salary-gap-with-hamilton-and-verstappen] The review of the incident will be an exercise in self criticism for McLaren. The team seeks to optimize its performance and prevent internal competition from costing them options in the championship. Stella trusts that the analysis will allow them to find areas of improvement in the management of duels between their drivers without giving up the philosophy of letting them compete. The constructors' championship is very tight and every point is vital. McLaren knows it cannot afford to lose opportunities due to a lack of coordination between its drivers. The review of the Monza duel will be key to establishing clearer guidelines for the future and ensuring that the ambition of Norris and Piastri translates into the best possible result for the team.

items.article_search_text: More teams are dissecting their performance at Monza, especially with the Spanish Grand Prix coming up. It has been a couple of days since Kimi Antonelli won [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/race-day/antonelli-makes-history-at-monza-and-wins-from-the-back] the 2026 Italian Grand Prix. And yet, teams around the F1 paddock are still analyzing what went wrong (and right) for them at the Temple of Speed. It's not a surprise, though. We had so much going on during the Italian GP that it's perfectly reasonable to talk about it days after. MCLAREN EXPLAINS HECTIC MONZA WEEKEND After a disappointing performance in the qualifying sessions, McLaren gave their fans a better show on Sunday. Reigning World Champion Lando Norris finished fourth, just a spot ahead of teammate Oscar Piastri. But the McLaren garage had a huge scare when Norris and Piastri came to blows in the latter stages of the race. Norris found himself on the grass at the exit of Curva Grande, but he still managed to come back and overtake Piastri in the final lap. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella had nothing negative to say about the battle between his two drivers. Instead, he applauded his team's resiliency in bouncing back from a difficult Saturday to a more productive Sunday. HADJAR OFFICIALLY SITS OUT AT MADRID As expected, Red Bull Racing has confirmed that Isack Hadjar will miss his third straight race [https://www.espn.ph/f1/story/_/id/49860811/isack-hadjar-miss-f1-spanish-gp-liam-lawson-continues-red-bull] weekend. Liam Lawson will continue to drive for Red Bull's main team at the Spanish Grand Prix, while reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda stays on with the Racing Bulls. Lawson is coming off a difficult Monza race, where he lost important time due to front-wing damage. Meanwhile, Tsunoda, who was just in his second race this season, came through with his first points in 2026 [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/2026-italian-grand-prix-surprises-and-busts-at-the-temple-of-speed]. RED BULL HAVING FUN AT THEIR ADUO DEMISE Instead of sulking in the corner, the Red Bull social team is having fun referencing their Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) ranking. Here's one of their tweets [https://x.com/redbullracing/status/2096977540808364109], if you need a bit of a laugh to start your day. Red Bull-Ford Powertrains, in their first year as the team's engine manufacturer, was found to have the best Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) in the F1 grid. It's a good testament to their work, but under the ADUO rules, it also left them without an additional opportunity to upgrade their engine. MEKIES REFLECTS ON RED BULL'S PODIUM FINISH Despite Max Verstappen's complaints about their straight-line speed, Red Bull still gained some ground with a P3 finish. They were able to stay ahead of the likes of McLaren and Ferrari, two teams that were expected to strongly contend for the podium places at Monza. Mekies said that they're in the "right direction," but they won't be satisfied until they find the "ultimate speed" they're looking for. Let's see if Verstappen and Liam Lawson can extract more pace at the Madring.
